title: Tracing & Dashboards: Weekly Handoff and Cost Telemetry Sync 2026-04-23
content:
Meeting date: 2026-04-23
Attendees: Aisha, Diego, Priya, Liam, Zoe (notes)
Duration: 45m standup-style sync + 15m deep-dive

Purpose:
- Weekly handoff for on-call + owners of tracing dashboards and cost telemetry.
- Capture action items, quick metrics snapshot, and small runbook edits before end of sprint.

Agenda:
1) Quick status from each area (traces, dashboards, pipeline costs)
2) Dashboard refresh rollouts (Grafana -> Observability Console)
3) Cost telemetry anomalies and short-term mitigations
4) Runbook/alert tuning follow-ups
5) Handoff notes for next-week on-call rotation

Notes / Highlights:
- Traces:
  - Diego: core tracing ingestion pipeline running at 95% throughput; a minor spike in dropped spans on 2026-04-21 between 03:10-03:24 UTC. Root cause likely brief GC pause on indexer node id=idx-03. Logs + JMX show memory pressure.
  - Action: add heap pressure alert to indexer SLOs (see below).

- Dashboards:
  - Priya: migrated three panels to the new metric schema in Observability Console (requests-by-model, kvcache-hit-rate, model-switch-fallbacks). Panels look good but the latency histogram needs a different binning to show long tails.
  - Decision: keep current panels live but push revised histogram config by Fri 2026-04-24.

- Cost telemetry:
  - Liam: token-cost aggregation job (daily rollup) underestimated GPU-hours for dedicated capacity because a recent model shard naming change bypassed mapper logic for ~12 hours on 2026-04-20. Rough incremental cost: +$1.8k for that day (est.).
  - Mitigation: backfill correct mapping and re-run rollup; temporary tag in dashboard to flag adjusted day.

Operational incidents and follow-ups:
- Incident (minor): dropped spans 2026-04-21 03:10-03:24 UTC.
  - Impact: 0.7% of total spans dropped; affected traces predominantly from hosted-api route /v1/generate in us-west1.
  - Root cause hypothesis: indexer GC on idx-03 + transient network packet loss between idx-03 and kafka-broker-2.
  - Next steps: Diego to gather GC logs and kernel dmesg from idx-03, create a short repro job to see if memory config needs bump. Owner: Diego. Due: 2026-04-25.

- Alert tuning:
  - Current p99 trace latency alert fires too often during scheduled nightly batch windows. We agreed to scope the alert to "user-facing" requests only (exclude nightly-batch label) and add a 3m cooldown. Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-04-26.

Metrics snapshot (quick, approximate):
- p95 end-to-end trace latency (hosted-api): 120ms
- p99 end-to-end trace latency (hosted-api): 480ms (long tail increased slightly vs last week)
- Span drop rate (last 7d): 0.35% (baseline 0.12%)
- Daily token-cost (hosted): ~$42k/day (observed variance +4% week-over-week)

Decisions made:
- Push histogram bin change and label filters to dashboards by EOD Fri (Priya).
- Add heap-pressure alert to indexer SLO and a network-latency monitor between indexers and brokers (Diego).
- Backfill cost rollup and annotate the week of 2026-04-20 on the cost dashboard (Liam).
- Update runbook alert wording to include delta-based suppression for scheduled jobs (Zoe + Aisha).

Action items (owner -> task -> due):
- Diego -> collect GC/dmesg logs from idx-03 and open a short investigation ticket with sample traces -> 2026-04-25
- Priya -> update histogram binning + alert scope change in Observability Console -> 2026-04-24
- Liam -> re-run cost rollup after mapping backfill; add dashboard annotation for 2026-04-20 -> 2026-04-24
- Zoe -> update runbook text for scheduled-job suppression (add examples) -> 2026-04-27
- Aisha -> perform on-call handoff notes and escalate to platform-eng if indexer memory needs a config change -> 2026-04-25

Runbook edits (short checklist to commit):
- Add new indexer heap pressure alert (severity P2) with play steps (restart indexer, capture heapdump, escalate to infra).
- Add note on suppression of p99 alerts during nightly batch windows and how to annotate scheduled jobs.
- Include a short paragraph on cost-telemetry backfills and when to annotate dashboards vs. patching rollups.

Open questions / discussion notes (unresolved):
- Should we aggregate cost telemetry at model-family level instead of shard to make anomalies noisier but cheaper to compute? Pros: lower cardinality, faster rollups. Cons: loses fine-grained chargebacks for product teams. Deferred to product-cost sync. (Owner: Liam to bring to Product Cost Sync 2026-04-29)
- Long-term: consider moving KV cache hit-rate sampling to a continuous metric (currently histogram sample) — affects storage and query costs. Priya to prototype next sprint.

Handoff summary for next-week on-call (quick):
- Watch for any spike in span drops; indexer idx-03 flagged until investigation closes.
- If cost rollup backfill increases daily cost by >5% compared to last 7-day avg, escalate to finance-gtm and tag customer-success for high spend customers.
- Dashboard changes are low-risk but verify the latency histogram after deployment (Priya will own verification window).

Notes to self / informal:
- "Remember to ping infra before bumping heap on indexers — coordinate maintenance window."
- Scratch: consider a short synthetic test that writes high-cardinality trace headers (to replicate mapper bypass).

Next sync: 2026-04-30 (same time) — agenda to include post-backfill cost numbers and indexer investigation status.

---
Document drafted by Aisha Khatri. Please add any missing context or edit runbook sections directly. If you comment in the doc, prefix with initials and date (AK 2026-04-23).
